artboards.title: B · two phones, wide fan, shorter card
D · three phones, widest fan, shortest card

annotations.text:
A · Sketch grid — the attached sketch, literally.
Two by two at every width, screenshots tilted and broken out of the card top. Reads as a toy shelf.
Tradeoff: at 390px the two-up cards leave ~150px of text width, so the blurbs have to be short — that is the least SEO copy of the three.

B · Marquee row — four abreast, editorial hero.
Left-aligned hero so the h1 and the paragraph read as one block; cards straight-on and equal weight.
Tradeoff: four equal cards say all four tools are equally real. Three of them are not.

C · Featured — the shipped tool leads.
The dex builder gets a split hero card with a real screenshot and a solid CTA; the other three sit in a supporting row.
Tradeoff: it buries the league builder, which is the tool with a settled spec and the next page to rank.

SEO structure, same in all three:
· h1 carries "make your own Pokédex" plus region and league.
· Each card is an <h2> that exactly matches its slug: /custom-pokedex-builder, /pokemon-league-builder, /favorite-pokemon-picker.
· The footer repeats the four links as anchor text.
Watch out: making / a router moves the dex builder off the URL that ranks today (~pos 7.8 for "pokedex builder").

D · Poster cards — four permutations of the fan, so pick one and we iterate on it.
Same page and same copy in all four; only the card differs. A and B use two phones, C and D use three. Left to right the fan gets wider and the red card gets shorter.
Each phone is a whole mobile viewport screenshot at its own proportions — nothing scaled or cropped — overhanging the card top and left, cut only by the card's bottom edge.

Why the tilt and the gradient are linked. The gradient is clipped to the card, so it has to be fully transparent below the height where the artwork starts hanging off the left — otherwise its hard left edge shows against artwork that keeps going.
Each phone rotates about its own top-left corner, so its left edge walks rightwards as it descends and crosses back inside the card at popLeft / sin(tilt) below its top. A steeper tilt crosses sooner and leaves more room for the gradient; a shallow tilt with a wide overhang leaves none. That is why the wider fans (B and D) can also be the shortest cards.
Four rules now fail the build rather than being caught by eye: the phone must outrun the card's bottom, leave at least 16% of the card bare on its right, clear the grid's top padding so row one does not land on the hero, and leave the gradient enough headroom.

The other two widths, both using permutation A. Desktop is the four mobile cards side by side, not a two-by-two.
Swap in whichever permutation you pick and these follow.
